Person x facet-level standardized-residual matrix

Source: R/api-plotting-secondary.R
plot_residual_matrix.Rd

Visualizes the person x element matrix of standardized residuals from diagnose_mfrm() as a heatmap. Complements plot(x, type = "guttman") (which shows raw responses) by exposing the residual structure directly: large positive cells show under-prediction, negative cells over-prediction.

Usage

plot_residual_matrix(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  facet = "Rater",
  top_n_persons = 40L,
  preset = c("standard", "publication", "compact", "monochrome"),
  draw = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

An mfrm_fit from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional diagnose_mfrm() output. Computed on demand when omitted.

facet

Facet whose levels become the column axis (default "Rater").

top_n_persons

Cap on the number of rows. Defaults to 40 to keep the figure legible; persons are kept by largest absolute residual mean.

preset

Visual preset.

draw

If TRUE, print the ggplot object.

Value

Invisibly, a ggplot object. plot_data(p) bundles the residual matrix (rows = Person, columns = facet level) and the long-form obs table.

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

Migration in 0.2.4

This renderer is internal. Use the corresponding plot() route in mfrmr_plot_migration; the former exported name is no longer available.

See also

plot(x, type = "guttman"), plot(x, type = "unexpected"), mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

# Supplementary workflow: run explicitly to keep routine checks brief.
# example("plot_residual_matrix", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
p <- plot(fit, type = "residual_matrix", top_n_persons = 12, draw = FALSE)
dim(plot_data(p, "matrix"))
# Look for: |residual| > 2 or > 3 crosses conventional two- or
#   three-standard-deviation review bands; these are heuristic screens,
#   not calibrated 5% or 1% tests (Wright & Linacre 1994). Repeated
#   high-magnitude cells at one facet level warrant pattern review but
#   do not by themselves establish scoring drift.
} # }
